workspace.name: Sample: Coastal adaptation
workspace.researchQuestion: How do coastal cities fund climate adaptation?

q-root.title: How do coastal cities fund climate adaptation?

card-wiki-adaptation.title: Climate change adaptation - Wikipedia
card-wiki-adaptation.summary: Overview of adaptation strategies, ecological infrastructure, and financial barriers for coastal municipalities.

highlights.quote: Coastal adaptation requires blended finance across municipal bonds, sovereign funds and international grants.

card-wiki-adaptation.note: Key introductory reading on adaptation definitions.

card-wiki-bonds.title: Green bond - Wikipedia
card-wiki-bonds.summary: Fixed-income financial instruments designed specifically to support climate-related or environmental projects.

highlights.quote: Municipal green bonds have expanded rapidly in Europe and North America to fund storm surge barriers.

card-wiki-bonds.note: Check difference between sovereign and municipal issuances.

card-oecd-finance.title: Financing Climate Adaptation in Cities - OECD
card-oecd-finance.summary: Policy framework assessing municipal capacity to leverage private sector capital for sea walls and flood defence.

highlights.quote: Only 12% of total climate finance reaches local governments directly.

card-oecd-finance.note: Crucial statistic to cite in the opening paragraph.

card-worldbank-resilience.title: Investing in Urban Resilience - World Bank
card-worldbank-resilience.summary: Economic analysis demonstrating that every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure yields four dollars in avoided damages.

highlights.quote: Every $1 invested in infrastructure resilience saves $4 over the asset lifecycle.

card-ipcc-report.title: IPCC AR6 WG2 Chapter 6: Cities, Settlements and Key Infrastructure
card-ipcc-report.summary: Sixth Assessment Report synthesis of global observed impacts, adaptation limits, and governance mechanisms in coastal deltas.

highlights.quote: Sea level rise will challenge traditional hard engineering, necessitating flexible spatial planning and insurance pools.

card-ipcc-report.note: Section 6.4 covers municipal adaptation finance gaps.

card-rotterdam-video.title: Rotterdam: Living With Water - Resilient Urban Design
card-rotterdam-video.summary: Documentary exploring the water square Benthemplein and subterranean car-park water storage solutions.

highlights.quote: Benthemplein functions as an amphitheatre during dry periods and collects 1.7 million litres of rainwater during storms.

card-rotterdam-video.note: Great visual case study of dual-purpose public spaces.

card-jakarta-sea-wall.title: Giant Sea Wall Jakarta: Megaproject Challenges
card-jakarta-sea-wall.summary: Investigative report on land subsidence, sea defence construction costs, and community relocation issues in North Jakarta.

highlights.quote: North Jakarta has sunk up to 2.5 metres in ten years due to unregulated groundwater extraction.

card-jakarta-sea-wall.note: Contrasting case: hard engineering barriers vs land subsidence.

card-venice-mose.title: MOSE Barrier System in Venice Lagoon
card-venice-mose.summary: Longitudinal operational analysis of mobile floodgates protecting Venice against record acqua alta high tides.

highlights.quote: Operational maintenance costs exceed 100 million euros annually, creating long-term fiscal burdens.

card-venice-mose.note: Operating expenditure vs initial capital expenditure problem.

card-standalone-insurance.title: Parametric Flood Insurance in the Caribbean - CCRIF
card-standalone-insurance.summary: Multi-country catastrophe risk pooling mechanism enabling rapid liquidity payouts post-hurricane.

highlights.quote: Parametric triggers pay out within 14 days of defined tropical storm windspeeds.

card-standalone-insurance.note: Novel financial instrument alternative to traditional disaster aid.

card-standalone-coastal-act.title: US Coastal Zone Management Act Evaluation
card-standalone-coastal-act.summary: National coastal resilience grant distribution across federal, state and tribal agencies.

card-note-synthesis.title: Synthesis: CapEx vs OpEx in Barrier Projects
card-note-synthesis.note: Hard coastal defences (like Venice MOSE) incur recurrent operational costs that strain city budgets. Nature-based solutions (like Rotterdam water squares) distribute costs across recreation and water utility budgets.

card-note-supervisor.title: Questions for Supervisor
card-note-supervisor.note:
1. Should we focus exclusively on OECD cities or contrast with Global South deltas?
2. Is green bond revenue transparency sufficient for quantitative analysis?
